To add a new gRPC method, add the gRPC method in xrp_ledger.proto. The method name should begin with a verb. Define the request and response types in their own file. The name of the request type should be the method name suffixed with `Request`, and the response type name should be the method name suffixed with `Response`. For example, the `GetAccountInfo` method has request type `GetAccountInfoRequest` and response type `GetAccountInfoResponse`.

After defining the protobuf messages for the new method, add an instantiation of the templated `CallData` class in GRPCServerImpl::setupListeners(). The template parameters should be the request type and the response type.

Finally, define the handler itself in the appropriate file under the src/ripple/rpc/handlers folder. If the method already has a JSON/Websocket equivalent, write the gRPC handler in the same file, and abstract common logic into helper functions (see Tx.cpp or AccountTx.cpp for an example).

ai.description: This file implements the core logic for registering, managing, and retrieving RPC handlers in the XRPL server. It defines utility templates for wrapping handler functions and for invoking handler implementations with version and role checks. The main class, HandlerTable, maintains a multimap of handler names to Handler objects, ensuring no overlapping API version ranges for the same handler name. It provides static access to the handler table, methods to retrieve handlers by name and API version (with beta support), and to list all handler names. The file also defines a static array of all built-in handlers, specifying their names, function pointers, required roles, and conditions. The design ensures that only valid handlers for the requested API version and role are accessible, supporting extensibility and versioning of the RPC interface.

This header file defines the structure and logic for handling RPC (Remote Procedure Call) methods in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. It introduces an enum for various conditions required to execute RPC handlers, such as network connectivity and ledger state. The core structure is the Handler, which associates an RPC method name, its implementation, required user role, and conditions. The file provides utility functions to retrieve handlers by name and version, generate JSON objects for responses, list available handler names, and check if the necessary conditions are met before executing a handler. The conditionMet function performs a series of checks on the application and network state to ensure the requested RPC can be processed, returning appropriate error codes if requirements are not satisfied.

This file implements the doSubscribe function, which handles the 'subscribe' RPC command in the XRPL server. The function processes subscription requests from clients, allowing them to receive real-time updates on various data streams such as server status, ledger changes, book changes, manifests, transactions, validations, peer status, consensus, and account-related events. It supports both WebSocket and URL-based subscriptions, with additional authentication for URL subscriptions (admin-only). The function validates input parameters, manages subscription objects, and sets up the requested streams or account/book monitoring. It also supports experimental features like account history transaction streams and can provide immediate snapshots of order books if requested. Error handling is included for malformed or unauthorized requests, and the function returns a JSON result summarizing the subscription status or any warnings.

It includes logic for accepting and handing off connections, authorizing requests, parsing and validating JSON-RPC requests (including batch requests), managing resource limits and roles, and generating appropriate HTTP or WebSocket responses. The file also provides setup utilities for configuring server ports, SSL contexts, and client/overlay endpoints based on configuration files. Error handling, logging, and request duration tracking are integrated throughout. The ServerHandler::Setup class and related functions help parse and apply server configuration. The code ensures secure, efficient, and standards-compliant handling of RPC traffic for the XRPL server.

This file implements the core logic for the 'tx' RPC handler in the XRPL (Ripple) server. It provides functionality to retrieve transaction details by transaction hash or CTID (Composite Transaction ID), optionally within a specified ledger range and in either binary or JSON format. The main workflow involves parsing and validating input parameters, fetching the transaction and its metadata from the ledger or transaction tables, determining if the transaction is validated, and constructing a detailed JSON response. The file defines helper structures (TxResult, TxArgs) to manage transaction query results and arguments, and includes functions for validation, transaction lookup (doTxHelp), response formatting (populateJsonResponse), and the main handler entry point (doTxJson). The handler supports both legacy and newer API versions, handles error cases (such as invalid parameters, wrong network, or transaction not found), and enriches the response with additional fields like delivered amount, NFT synthetic data, and CTID when available.
